\n- owns: `<sub>/heartbeats/<name>`;

\nThe platform reads `worker`, `ts`, `status[].id`, `status[].phase`, `status[].epoch`, `status[].revision`, `status[].observed_revision`, `server`, `instance`, `labels`, the capacity and the headroom; the rest are words of the subsystem that the platform does not read (`heartbeat.strings` of the manifest names which of them are strings).
\n**`heartbeat.worker`** — equal to the name in the key
\n**`heartbeat.ts`** — for display and for the clock divergence, not for freshness
\n**`heartbeat.status`** — one element per unit that the worker runs
\n**`heartbeat.status[]`, `phase: sealed`** — revision — of the read row;
\n**`heartbeat.status[]`, `phase: sealed`** — not a claim on the unit (P/08.1 N1.6 claim) and not «running» (P/06.5)
\n**`heartbeat.status[]`, `phase: unreadable`** — why «row unreadable: `<reason>`»;
\n**`heartbeat.status[]`, `phase: unreadable`** — revision — if the revision of the row is readable;
\n**`heartbeat.status[]`, `phase: unreadable`** — not a claim and not «running»
\nThe only subsystem word in that testsub status element is n, the current counter value; the book tallies of the testsub manifest shows n. That element has no other subsystem words.
\n**`heartbeat.fetched`** — no field or empty — nothing is reported;
\n**`heartbeat.fetched`** — the length is bounded by FETCHED_COUNT/FETCHED_BYTES (the request mark contract «fetched»)
\n**`heartbeat.<capacity.from>`** is emitted when the capacity is known.
\n**`heartbeat.<headroom.from>`** — the base computes capacity − Σ of the assignment weights, the subsystem MAY say its own value, the base does not overwrite it, like schema, build;
\n**`heartbeat.<headroom.from>`** — the controller does not read the field;

\nFor **`heartbeat.<headroom.from>`**, each unit weight follows the pool contract as at the controller: use weight.field of the unit row read by the last reconciliation; an absent field uses weight.default, and absent placement.weight means 1.
\nFor **`heartbeat.<headroom.from>`**, a unit whose selected weight field is not a number does not enter the sum (the controller does not place that unit, P/04).
\n**`heartbeat.<place_by>`** — written by the base, not by the subsystem
\n**`heartbeat.fenced`** — after «release_name» the heartbeat is not written
\n**`heartbeat.was_fenced`** — the series worker_fenced{worker} of P/06.5
\n**`heartbeat.place_error`** — a closed list of words;
\n**`heartbeat.place_error`** — the record is removed when the place is taken or let go;
\n**`heartbeat.place_error`** — there are no more records than candidate places;
\nThe **`heartbeat.place_error`** field does not change `<place_by>`: it remains the held place name or "" by P/03.4-R053.
\n**`heartbeat.freeing`** — 0 — frees nothing;
\n**`heartbeat.freeing`** — what to free — the subsystem;
\n**`heartbeat.freeing`** — no field — 0
\n**`heartbeat.schema, build, pending_writes`** — pending_writes := 0 when the subsystem did not supply it;
\n**`heartbeat.schema, build, pending_writes`** — no pending_writes field — the drain is not safe
\n**`heartbeat.stood_in`** — as_of — ts of the last heartbeat of the loop that the stand-in repeats (the age of the subsystem state), the same at the next repeats;
\n**`heartbeat.stood_in`** — ts of the heartbeat — the time of this repeat
\n**`heartbeat.command_counts`** — the metric — command_counts.`<outcome>`
\n**`heartbeat.command_road`** — by — operator or the subsystem of the filer (the first part of the stamp by «`<sub>/<unit>`» of a request filed by a worker, chapter 3.6 N1.5)
\n**`heartbeat.command_request`** — from filed (the instance row) the time is not derived
\n**`heartbeat.command_wait`** — command_request ≈ command_road + command_wait
\n**`heartbeat.filings.again`** counts the same request filed again.
\n**`heartbeat.filings.refused`** counts requests not filed.
\n**`histogram.buckets`** — [`<count>`…] — one per boundary of ROAD_BUCKETS, the count of observations not greater than the boundary (cumulative)
\n**`histogram.sum`** — `<sum of seconds>`;
\n**`histogram.count`** — `<number of observations>`.
\nWhen the unit's launch backoff has not reached RETRY_MAX or its count has been reset, the heartbeat has no `status[].stalled` field for that unit.
\n**`phase.rule`** — the platform knows three — running (the counter running, the neighbourhood near), sealed and unreadable — the elements above
\n**`cadence.fresh_for`** — the reader judges by the change on its own clock
\n**`platform_strings`** — url — (P/06.5 N3 «/where/`<id>`»: the url of the door);
\n**`platform_strings`** — fetched — (chapter 3.6 N3 «holder's look»)
\nAn empty or invalid `SERVER_NAME` gives the existing startup refusal, exit 2: this start has no lock, capture or heartbeat.

\n`LEASE_TTL`, `LEASE_MARGIN` and the other lease timings, the rival marks and the places — [chapter 3.2](03.2-worker.norms.md) N1.2; the loop timings (`loop`, `watchdog`) — [chapter 3.3](03.3-worker.norms.md) N1.2.
\n**`stand_in.FOR`** — it does not stand in longer: the units go

\n**`memory.rule`** is not checked without unit_mb, CAPACITY or WORKER_MEMORY_MB. The capacity is capacity.default; a domain worker has no role file and has no values. There is one budget formula per module: CAPACITY is the worker capacity in weight units (the pool contract capacity); unit_mb is MiB per weight unit, base_mb is MiB for the process (absent means 0), and WORKER_MEMORY_MB comes from the process environment.
\nThe worker side of the declared-table rules is P/03.4-R012, P/03.4-R099, P/03.4-R100 and P/03.4-R183 through P/03.4-R193.
\nThe console is the writer of `<sub>/<t>/<name>` table rows, except for the worker tables declared in `worker.writes`; those follow P/03.4-R184.
\nFor a worker table declared in `worker.writes`, the worker does not delete rows by term.
\nIn a whole-row worker-table write, the worker base writes the platform field `revision`; the subsystem does not set it.
\nOn a cas conflict of a whole-row worker-table write, reread the row and compute `revision` anew by P/03.4-R099.
\nDuring startup resealing of a list-form worker table under P/03.4-R100, a cas conflict requires a reread; a second worker that sees the new kid does not write.

\nDuring startup resealing of a list-form worker table under P/03.4-R100, skip an unreadable row with a log line and continue startup. A worker table with declared fields `*_secret` still causes a load refusal.
\nThe console door of the cluster has its own norm (P/06.3, P/06.5), not this one.
\nDOOR_* are independent owned rows in runtime-constants.tsv.
\nThe process-door busy refusal of P/03.4-R104 includes `Retry-After` with a delay of DOOR_BUSY_RETRY_AFTER seconds.
\n**`door_limits.body`** — DOOR_BODY_BYTES;
\nThe process-door limits have no manifest setting; a door needing different settings names them in its own lesson (P/03.4-R107).
\nAfter `ambiguous`, the worker repeats the write with the same `id`.
\nAfter `unavailable`, the worker repeats the write as it is.
\nNeither a lease nor the silence ceiling allows publishing the control state: only a live own slot.
\nAn own renewal (including one by the stand-in) keeps holder/gen and the name; a change of the holder or of the generation is a loss.
\nThe stand-in still renews the slot and permitted strict place and repeats the heartbeat by P/03.4-R019; its strict-place renewal remains a write under the slot guard.
\nThe token is issued by the console — [P/06.5](../../06-console/spec/06.5-console.norms.md) N3 «`/where/<id>`».
\nIts columns `word`, `cause`, `outcome`, `diagnostic`, `caller` are the normative cells of a refusal, the rows in file order; `-` is an absent cell.
\nMachine columns identify the surface and any fixed code.
\nA `peer` surface refers to the imported door contract; it creates no HTTP API of the worker.
\nGoverning rules and the public acceptance scope remain in this chapter.
\nHeartbeats and marks need a separate observer/stand or a reading of the implementation by its owner; the author's review of documents is not such evidence.
